title: Confinement
text: “Sigh... Itsuki really is so single-minded—or rather, once he decides he’s right, he won’t listen to anyone else.”
“However, I’ve heard that in the future, around this time, he was investigating the Three Heroes Church with Ren, trying to get to the bottom of things.”

“I think he just won’t listen once he’s convinced the other side is evil. Maybe it’s because Ren was there at the time? Otherwise, he probably wouldn’t realize it unless the Three Heroes Church actually attacked us. If it were just us… even if we brought Melty-chan along, he’d probably start saying she’s been brainwashed or something.”
That’s definitely true.
“I guess Itsuki is pure—or rather, arrogant—in a different way than Motoyasu-kun.”
“Am I arrogant?”

“Arrogant… or maybe just single-minded? According to Motoyasu-kun, he stubbornly trusts his comrades and won’t budge. That’s why he kept getting deceived by that Bitch princess, but Itsuki won’t compromise on the justice he believes in. Even if there are some odd points to it… he thinks everything will be resolved as long as he defeats evil.”
I see. In that sense, you could say he’s strong-willed. Pushing forward on the path you believe in does, in a way, require courage.
“Maybe having the drive to take action is a quality of a hero… I suppose. It’s just that, no matter how many times he goes through the loop, it just ends up spinning his wheels.”
Suddenly, my Father gazes off into the distance.

“Why is it that we… can’t seem to understand each other at all? I think the future me… will surely be a far stronger person than I am now. Trying to understand someone like Itsuki—or Ren, who only sees things within the limits of what he knows—I think I’d just give up.”
“What are you saying? You’re a wonderful person, Father.”
“That’s right, bro! Thanks to you, everyone was saved, and that’s why the revolution is moving forward like this. I think if you just talk to them, they’ll listen.”
Keel cheerfully encouraged my father. I agree, too.
“I… want to believe that…”
For some reason, my father muttered, looking very exhausted. His back looks so worn down. Ah, am I failing to be a support for my Father? I really want to find a way to help him.
“I want to believe Itsuki is safe. For now… it doesn’t look like we can just let Itsuki go. It seems we’ll have no choice but to keep him confined until this commotion is over.”
Father muttered in a weary voice.
“Is that so? Torture?”
“To make him confess to something?”

My Assistant and my Rival asked in unison, echoing Father. Hmm, for someone of dragon blood, that’s actually a pretty good idea. Torturing Itsuki, brainwashing him, and turning him into an ally isn’t a bad move at all.
“No way!”
“You’re not going to do what Kou did? You mean, threaten him?”
“I’d like to ask Gaelion-chan why she thought I’d resort to threats.”
“Well, Naofumi is really good at discipline. Gaelion thinks Naofumi is so cool when he does that. It’s especially effective on the Bow Hero.”
This Rival! To top it all off, she’s laughing as she recalls the time my Father disciplined Kou! Should I finish him off right now? Huh!?
“Gyaa! I’m scared of being dismembered!”
Kou let out a scream from outside the room. I rushed out to calm him down. After all, since the room has been turned into a dragon’s sanctuary, it’s pretty stressful for him…

“Torture, you see. It works on some people and not on others. Kou says he doesn’t want to die and feels remorse for what he did, but with Itsuki, he prioritizes injustice over remorse and justice over his life—he just sees torture as another form of adversity, so it doesn’t work on him.”
“Is that so?”
“Ugh… He’s completely beyond help. This creepy, short guy.”
“It doesn’t sound very convincing coming from little, cute Keel-kun, though.”
“What did you say!?”
Hmm, Father’s point is valid, I suppose. However, as far as I’m concerned, I think Itsuki would break within a few days if we tortured him.
“Clashes of ideology tend to be like that. To persuade him, he’d have to witness the Queen punishing Trash or get trapped by the Three Heroes Church—otherwise, it’s impossible.”
“Is it really okay to let her do something like that?”

“We can’t exactly make her do that… Well, if Motoyasu and I went along and stormed a Three Heroes Church… she might believe us. Those guys probably think they can get away with anything as long as they defeat me, so they’d probably just cut Itsuki loose without a second thought after he loses to Motoyasu.”
“That’s a brilliant idea! Let’s do it!”
Keel blurts out, seizing the opportunity.
“If we do something like that, the revolution will accelerate with the momentum of crushing the Three Heroes Church! Think about Melty-chan for a second.”
“Ah… you’re right. Well then, big bro… this is gonna be a huge hassle.”
“Yeah. Once it’s gone this far, even Motoyasu-kun’s knowledge of the future won’t be of any use…”
And so, our days of keeping Itsuki imprisoned passed by like that.
One day has passed since we confined Itsuki. Since the loop would restart if he died of starvation, we decided to feed him.
“Itsuki, it’s time to eat.”
“I won’t accept charity from evil!”
“Just eat it already!”
“Yikes!”
I shoved the food that Father had made right into Itsuki’s mouth. Then, seeing how much pain Itsuki was in, I splashed water on him to rehydrate him.
“Torture?”
“Is it?”
My Assistant and my Rival are saying something. By the way, these two are acting as guards. They’re the ones capable of dispelling Itsuki’s Magic and interfering with his teleportation.
“Guh! Guh!　“Do you really think you can get away with doing something like this?!”
“It’s because you won’t eat it willingly. You should actually be grateful just to be given a meal! That’s right.”
“If you won’t let me eat it, I’ll just ask for more next time.”
“I won’t do that. My Father would get mad at me.”
“You people…!”
Time passes in a scene like that. By the way, as expected, Itsuki didn’t believe his Finacée’s story. It seems they’re brushing everything off as brainwashing.

In fact, his fiancée said it looked more like the Bow Hero was the one being brainwashed. It’s frustrating, but I have to agree. Incidentally, at that moment, my Father had a rather ambiguous expression on his face.
And so, four days have passed since we confined Itsuki. So far, no assassins from the Three Heroes Church have come to our hideout. Not that we couldn’t fight them off if they did come.

Itsuki is being guarded by me, my Assistant, and my Rival. Filolial-sama and the others are taking turns keeping watch outside. Is the revolutionary movement in Melromarc finally coming to an end? I wonder if the Pope is about to lose patience and launch a surprise attack on us.
Just as I was thinking this, my Father arrived via portal from Siltvelt. He looked rather flustered.
“What’s the matter?”
“It’s terrible! I figured out why Siltvelt had been so quiet!”
My Father looked more frantic than I’d ever seen him before.
“Has Takt occupied the country? That would certainly be a different future from what we envisioned.”
“No, no! Things over there are surprisingly quiet, actually!”
“Then what happened?”
“The folks in Siltvelt got the wrong idea—they thought I was trying to overthrow the country—and they’ve mobilized their army! Right toward Melromarc, which is already in shambles!”
“What?!”

Come to think of it, that explains why Siltvelt’s castle town was so quiet. Trash… The prestige of the Wise King has faded, and on top of that, the movement to worship the Shield Hero is gaining momentum within the country. They must have begun their advance determined not to let the path my Father—the Shield Hero—had carved out go to waste.

“I was walking toward the town, thinking something was off, when a faction seeking to build friendship between Siltvelt and Melromarc approached me. They said that even within the country, people were secretly organizing troops to support the Shield Hero—taking all sorts of arbitrary actions on their own.”
“That’s a serious situation. What should we do…?”

In other words, this amounts to nothing less than launching an invasion of Melromarc under the guise of a revolutionary movement. I’ve heard that within Melromarc, many citizens have already converted to the Shield Faith, which worships the Shield Hero. They might even willingly accept Siltvelt’s rule. Could this be the reason the Queen is unable to return?
“So what should we do? Should I, Motoyasu, render the Siltvelt army incapable of fighting?”
“If you do that, the Three Heroes Church in Melromarc will see it as an opportunity and invade. Once that happens, the war will be unstoppable.”
My Father furrowed his brow in distress and paused for a moment.
“It’s already… as if the war has already begun. I think our only option is to find a way to minimize the damage as much as possible.”
“What about Faubrey and the surrounding nations?”
“Half are watching the situation unfold, and half are siding with one side or the other… the balance is leaning slightly toward Siltvelt.”
“At this rate, Melromarc will be destroyed.”

But isn’t that for the best? I’m sorry to my Finacée, but if this means a country like this surrenders to Siltvelt without a fight, I don’t think it’s a bad move. After all, the majority of the people are already on my Father’s side.

“After Siltvelt occupies the country, if my Father declares that he won’t tolerate discrimination against Demi-Humans and humans—and calls it the ‘Siltvelt Human Protection State’—it might not be a problem. Placing the queen and my Finacée there would solve everything.”

“That’s one option, sure. But Melty and I have already made a promise… to keep relations between our countries friendly. I think Melromarc and Siltvelt can only truly understand each other on an equal footing once we’ve gotten past this.”

Good heavens, Father is choosing the difficult path of mutual understanding between the two nations, rather than one side emerging victorious. I, Motoyasu, am so moved by Father’s strong commitment to peace that I can’t stop crying.
“I’m going to go warn the Siltvelt army to halt their advance. I think they’ll probably stop… but we’re running out of time. I’ve heard the Siltvelt army is about to reach the Melromarc border. So—”
Just then, a message arrow was stuck into the wall in front of our hideout.
